knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Each product is checked against the exact product and formulation requirements before use, so an apparently similar product is not assumed to be suitable.

The lesson says the approved products register records, for each product, the supplier, the product name and version, the formulation or composition reference, the SDS date, the approved uses and the storage requirements.

practicalCriteria: Learner checks a supplied product against the approved list and records the procurement decision with the label and SDS on file.
Learner decants a product into a clean, suitable container and labels it with product identifier, hazards, date and initials.
Learner stores stock labelled, closed and separated by incompatibility, and rotates the oldest product first.
Learner completes a stock check that records stock on hand, expiry dates and damaged containers.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Procurement approval record with label, SDS and cost basis
Stock register showing stock on hand, expiry dates and usage
Decanting record with product, container, date and initials
stopWorkCriteria: Learner decants into a food or drink container
Learner buys or uses a product with no SDS on file
Learner leaves a decanted container unlabelled
